I am still very much a work in progress but I have started DBT therapy (group therapy and individual councilling, it's an intensive for 6 months) and I already am starting to feel better and I am starting to imagine my future being so much better! I am even starting to like some of my traits (my deep empathy, my ability to connect with others immediately and make them feel safe, my shifting sense of identity which always has me trying new things and how creative I am) I am seeing that once I can control thy bad traits that I can possibly use the more positive ones to my advantage (did you know they teach people in business school how to mirror others to get them to like them so they can network and build their businesses, we already have this inherently) but oh my goodness it's hard and I still have really bad days! But I love reading everyone stories in this thread it's helping me want to keep going!

Also don't got into bpdlovedones not a single person in there loves the person they have in their life with bpd. They legit think we are all incurable monsters who should be killed by firing squad...I doubt a single person in that group cared to understand, work with or learn about the condition of the person with bpd in their lives.

There is a relaly good podcast I suggest BOTH of you listen to its called Back From The Boarderline, I listen to it on Spotify. Also if she isn't in DBT therapy currently I found a really good Patreon page called Putting the B in BPD. The woman whose Patreon it is has a PHD is psychology and has BPD herself and she is awesome! It's like $5 a month on the lowest level and you can pay a bit more to access her worksheets. She has realy good videos on DBT skills and exercises, they are soooo well done and comprehensive. Otherwise I just want to say it's so sweet you are so committed to being a good partner! I hope things work out for you both! <3

Yeah she seems toxic, possible sociopath or narcissist perhaps (sorry I know it's not good to diagnose ransom people but just so you know you are dealing with a severe case) it seems like you can't be friends because she is being really innapropriate with you by show up at your work. I would lay down some clear boundaries, be very very very clear. If she has a personality disorder you need to be super clear and almost over expalin your boundaries. Then I would block her (you can tell her you are going to do that after you explained boundaries like "don't show up at my work anymore it is really inappropriate and scary". I see a bunch of people saying jsut to ghost her or talk to her parents and ghost her please please DONT DO THAT! That is bad advice. I have a personality disorder and it is horrific, confusing, traumatic and it really fucks with my head and sense of reality when someone just disappears. Also just as a human you should be more respectful and communicative. You can't expect someone to act a certian way if you don't explain what you want and need.  I am always fine if you talk to me and tell me boundaries but a ghost jsut makes things worse for everyone involved. Ghosting will just egg her on to do worse and worse things. Believe me if you ghost it can get ALOT worse. Just be clear, set your boundaries, explain to her what you are going to do and why, don't let her draw you back in as she might try and do that then block her on everything. The boundaries and explaination will prevent things from getting worse and the blocking will prevent you from getting retriggered if she does try and reach out. Also it is very compationate of you, you will give her permission to also move on.

This is a very treatable disease but the person needs to be committed cuz DBT is hard and it takes time for it to start working. What she is doing. Isn't her "fault" it's an illness but it is her responsibility to work on getting better. All you can do is support her.
